questions.questionText: In a mangrove ecosystem, leaves from the grey mangrove plants fall into the water and sink to the mud below. They are then broken down by bacteria and fungi. Invertebrates such as crabs, prawns, and molluscs live in the mud and feed on the dead leaves. The bullseye fish feeds on the invertebrates. Humans eat prawns, crabs and fish. Herons and other wading birds live and breed in the mangroves. These birds feed on invertebrates and fish. What is correct about this ecosystem?

options.A: Bacteria, fungi, crabs, prawns and molluscs form the community in the mud.
options.B: Bullseye fish are at the second trophic level in the food web.
options.C: Fungi in the water are the main producers in the ecosystem.
options.D: Grey mangroves are the ecological niche of herons.

questions.questionText: Two species of birds feed on different insects living on the same tree and so do not compete for food. Which statement describes these two species of birds?

options.A: They occupy different habitats in the same ecosystem.
options.B: They occupy the same habitat in the same ecosystem.
options.C: They occupy different niches in the same habitat.
options.D: They occupy the same niche in the same habitat.
